name: רְאוּבֵן
summary: Jacob’s firstborn, by Leah, and the tribe that came from him, which camped south of the tabernacle at the head of its own camp and set out under Elizur son of Shedeur (Num 2:10; 10:18), and settled east of the Jordan with Gad (Num 32). The name is רְאוּ “see!” and בֵּן “a son”; Leah gives the reason with the verb of the root: “because Yahweh has looked on (רָאָה בְּ) my affliction; now my husband will love me” (Gen 29:32). He lost the firstborn’s place for going up to his father’s bed (Gen 35:22; 49:3–4; 1Ch 5:1), yet Moses blesses him, “Let Reuben live and not die” (Deu 33:6), and his name is on a gate of Ezekiel’s city and among the sealed tribes (Ezk 48:31; Rev 7:5).

evidence.note: “Leah conceived and bore a son, and called his name רְאוּבֵן, for she said, Because Yahweh has looked on my affliction (רָאָה יַהְוֶה בְּעָנְיִי); for now my husband will love me.”
The same seeing of affliction: “I have surely seen the affliction of my people.”
Reuben delivers Joseph out of his brothers’ hands, meaning to bring him back to his father.
Reuben lay with Bilhah his father’s concubine, and Israel heard.
“Reuben, you are my firstborn, my might and the first of my strength … unstable as water, you shall not excel, because you went up to your father’s bed.”
Because he defiled his father’s couch, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph.
The standard of the camp of Reuben on the south, under Elizur son of Shedeur.
“The standard of the camp of Reuben set out by their hosts, and over his host was Elizur son of Shedeur.”
Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, rose with Korah.
Reuben and Gad, with much cattle, saw the land of Jazer and Gilead and asked for it.
Reuben, Gad and half Manasseh built by the Jordan an altar “great to the sight (לְמַרְאֶה)”.
“Among the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart. Why did you sit among the sheepfolds?”
“Let Reuben live and not die, and let his men be few.”
The first of the north gates of the city, the gate of Reuben.
Of the tribe of Ῥουβήν twelve thousand were sealed.

note: Takes t.ab.ap (the name, 72 tokens) and the gentilic רְאוּבֵנִי (t.ab.aq, 18 tokens), which TIPNR lists as a form of Reuben@Gen.29.32. The text spells the gentilic both הָרֻאוּבֵנִי and הָראוּבֵנִי; the Septuagint and New Testament write Ῥουβήν. The reading “see, a son” takes the name as the imperative רְאוּ plus בֵּן; Leah’s own explanation (Gen 29:32) plays on רָאָה בְּעָנְיִי rather than spelling it out, so the gloss rests on the form and her reason together. t.ab.ap also counts the tribe and its land (Jos 13:15–23).
